item.title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
item.description: Bloomberg Mideast geoeconomics lead Dina Esfandiary tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a protracted Iran war, marked by cycles of escalation and pauses in fighting, is a key scenario as deep divisions over the Strait of Hormuz complicate diplomacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
item.description: China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Xi Summit Leaves Big Issues Unresolved
item.description: Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Stephen Engle tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping bought more time to negotiate over trade while major disagreements involving Taiwan, Iran and technology remain. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Engle explains how competition over AI and unresolved economic and security issues are shaping the next phase of US-China relations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Says China to Buy 10 Million Tons of Coal in 2027, 2028
item.description: China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US next year and again in 2028, according to the White House, in a sign of further progress in easing trade frictions between the world’s two largest economies.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Billionaire Charoen’s Asset World Targets $1 Billion REIT IPO
item.description: Asset World Corp Pcl’s new Thai Real Estate Investment Trust aims to raise at least $1 billion through a listing as it seeks funds to expand its hotel and commercial property business, according to a senior executive.
item.dc:creator: Anuchit Nguyen

item.title: Blackstone Cements Shift From Star Dealmakers With Baratta Exit
item.description: If there was any doubt that Jon Gray is now the center of gravity at Blackstone Inc., the past few weeks have erased it.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Singh and Dawn Lim

item.title: Wall Street Week | China’s Trade Reckoning, Syracuse’s Second Chance, Humanoids in Healthcare
item.description: This week, Council on Foreign Relations President Michael Froman breaks down China's export machine, why twenty years of US pressure hasn't worked, and what happens next. And, can a $100 billion Micron factory transform Syracuse from a Rust Belt cautionary tale into a potential model for American reindustrialization? Plus, a bridge named for a hockey legend was meant to strengthen the supply chain between the US and Canada, but the neighbors can’t agree on their trade relationship. Later, with 760,000 care aide openings expected every year in the US and a $400 billion long-term care bill, humanoid robots are an early bet on technology filling the care gap. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ellison Pledges $9.2 Billion More in Oracle Shares for Loans
item.description: Larry Ellison, a key figure behind Paramount Skydance Corp.’s deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., has pledged 67 million more shares of Oracle Corp. as collateral for personal loans than he had at the same time last year.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Palmeri and Brody Ford

item.title: Search for the Next Leader of the UN
item.description: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres' term ends this year, and three Security Council straw polls have provided no consensus. Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett is one of the top contenders. She speaks to Bloomberg Businessweek Daily about why she wants the job, and how she views the UN's role in the world moving forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Keeneland CEO on Annual Yearling Sale
item.description: Shannon Arvin says Keeneland’s yearling sale is running ahead of last year’s pace and is on track to top $550 million, making it the largest horse sale in the world. She said the auction is already up 3% to 4% this year after increasing by 24% last year, reflecting strong demand and continued interest in horse racing. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jev, an AI Model That Can’t Chat, Takes On Bigger Rivals
item.description: Jev, an AI model built by a former OpenAI researcher, went viral over the past week with the promise of a cheaper and faster alternative to large language models. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investing For The Great Wealth Transfer: Masters In Business
item.description: Barry speaks with Adam Frank, Managing Director and Head of Wealth Planning and Advice at J.P. Morgan Wealth Management. They discuss his time at Bear Stearns as the company was acquired by J.P. Morgan Chase, as well as his start in law before pivoting to wealth planning. They discuss building trust with clients to help them with diversification, as well as providing tax advice to help them save their money. They also discuss J.P. Morgan's new program for athletes, the J.P. Morgan Chase Athlete Council, which helps athletes, from student to pro, create and keep their wealth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street’s ‘80/20’ Shift Finds Fresh Fuel in Stock Bounceback
item.description: Wall Street spent another week watching yields hit multi-decade highs, oil hold above $100 and the case for tighter Federal Reserve policy harden. Once again, risk assets refused to break.
item.dc:creator: Vildana Hajric

item.title: The Tiny Magnet Maker That Attracted $1.6 Billion From Lutnick
item.description:
In late January, the week before Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced a $1.6 billion government commitment to fund a US magnet maker, bankers at his former financial services company, now run by his sons, were busy earning fees raising $1.5 billion more for the company from private investors.
The parallel deals have been questioned by Democratic lawmakers alleging possible conflicts of interest involving Lutnick and his sons. But a more basic set of questions has dogged the project: Can USA Rare Earth Inc., the company getting these public and private funds, actually produce the critical minerals and magnets the government needs to break China’s chokehold on global supplies?
For a closer look, we speak with Joe Deaux, Bloomberg News Senior Reporter for Corporate & Economic Statecraft. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Great Bond Shakeout Locks In a 5% World ‘Until Something Breaks’
item.description: As yields on US Treasuries soar past one high after the next, a reality is sinking in deeper across Wall Street and Washington: More than merely a bond-market slump, this might just be a fundamental shift. Myriad forces have combined to push the government’s borrowing costs higher — from $100-a-barrel oil and the AI spending boom, to yawning US budget deficits adding to a record $40 trillion debt load — all against a backdrop of a Federal Reserve bent on cooling inflation that’s run well past target for years. The selling pressure intensified this week as energy prices surged anew and data showed US businesses are humming along, giving an already hawkish central bank more reasons to keep raising interest rates. For a closer look, we speak with Kelsey Berro, Fixed Income Portfolio Manager at JPMorgan Asset Management. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taylor Swift To Debut 'Patient Zero' at VMAs
item.description: Bloomberg's Christina Ruffini joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Taylor Swift's new song 'Patient Zero' and new music video debuting this weekend at the MTV Video Music Awards. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SK Hynix’s Solidigm Is Said to Weigh US IPO as Soon as 2027
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s Solidigm is considering a US initial public offering as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz

item.title: Dollar’s Best Run Since March Has Wall Street Rethink View
item.description: The dollar wrapped up its best two-week stretch in six months, a sharp reversal that Wall Street strategists say could keep the currency supported through year end.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova and Naomi Tajitsu

item.title: Stocks Climb as Oil Retreats on US-Iran Deal Hopes: Markets Wrap
item.description: Hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough in the Iran war drove oil prices lower, fueling a rebound in stocks and easing the Treasury volatility that has roiled financial markets around the world.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: David Booth on Investing, Dimensional and Staying Calm | The David Rubenstein Show
item.description: David Booth started Dimensional Fund Advisors out of a Brooklyn brownstone in 1981 with an idea that challenged conventional investing: investors should have exposure to smaller companies as part of a diversified portfolio. Today, Dimensional manages more than $1 trillion. Booth sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss his new book, "Stay Calm," which applies his investment philosophy of staying calm during periods of market volatility, to navigating the uncertainties of life. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded August 10 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
